subject: MSA governing law & temporary injunctive relief — seat mapping + escalation matrix
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@harborai.com>, procurement@harborai.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA governing law & temporary injunctive relief — seat mapping + escalation matrix

Alex / HarborAI team — thanks again for the productive call this morning. Two items from our side that would speed redlines to execution: a clear seat (court) mapping for injunctive relief and an escalation matrix for legal approvals.

Quick summary of our proposal (covers both MSA and order form):
- Governing law: California (we prefer CA to keep consistency across hosted service contracts).
- Primary dispute resolution: binding arbitration for claims under $5M; venue for arbitration in San Francisco.
- Emergency equitable relief carve-out: we can agree a narrowly scoped carve-out that allows either party to seek temporary injunctive/provisional relief in a local court, but we need a deterministic seat-mapping and a short process for escalation/notice.

Operational asks: can HarborAI confirm the list of jurisdictions where you would claim injunctive relief (HQ + top 3 operating countries)? I attached a draft Seat-Mapping-Table that we use internally — if you populate it we’ll draft the exact clause mapping seats to the carve-out.

Legal asks (Kimberly / Marissa / David): please prepare two versions of the clause for internal review: (1) narrow carve-out limited to preservation of IP, CARTA/data-exfiltration, and urgent export-control blocks; (2) broader carve-out that includes availability/sla-critical outages. Include a short escalation matrix: who on Redwood legal signs off for each severity and expected 24–48 hour turntimes.

Attachments: HarborAI_MSA_redline_v3.docx (our starting redline), Seat-Mapping-Table.xlsx (please fill by EOD Monday).

Alex — if you can populate the seat table and confirm HarborAI’s legal POC, we’ll get the redline language ready for your counsel.

Best,
Sean

--
Sean Gallagher
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0192

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 9 Aug 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA governing law & temporary injunctive relief — seat mapping + escalation matrix

Sean — thanks for the clear ask. Two points from legal:
1) Scope of carve-out: I agree we should draft both narrow and broad options. For the narrow version we should be explicit that the carve-out is "solely to preserve evidence, prevent exfiltration of customer data, or to preserve trade secrets/AI model weights." That limits forum-shopping risk.
2) Territory mapping: instead of "up to top 3 operating countries" let's request HarborAI specify (i) HQ seat, (ii) any country where they maintain significant customer operations (>1000 users), and (iii) any entity-level subsidiaries that require local injunctive relief. That makes the seat table defensible.

David — can you prepare a 2-paragraph playbook for ops/legal on when to permit Redwood to seek injunctive relief in the customer's preferred seat (vs. insist on CA)? We should include a fallback: if the customer's preferred seat is not an option because of enforceability risk, the escalation matrix should require redwood legal + commercial approval to accept.

I’ll draft both clause options and upload a redline by EOD tomorrow.

-Kim

Sean / Redwood team — thanks, this is helpful. A few clarifying notes from HarborAI legal/procurement:
- HarborAI HQ is Wilmington, DE; primary engineering hubs are Boston (US) and Amsterdam (EU). For injunctive relief we typically request Delaware or Massachusetts depending on the remedy sought.
- Our counsel will likely press for Delaware as the preferred seat for preliminary injunctions tied to corporate governance or IP. For emergency data-exfiltration they prefer local courts where the affected subsidiary is located.

We can populate the Seat-Mapping-Table by EOD Monday (I’ll ask Maya in procurement to complete the operational rows). Couple questions:
1) Does Redwood have a preferred short-form clause that allows only "preservation" relief (temporary relief to preserve evidence/data) vs "remedial" relief (ordering performance/stop-service)? We prefer preservation-only language.
2) Timeline: once you upload the two clause options, what is a realistic internal approval window? Our counsel has asked for a committed 3–5 business day review for narrow carve-outs.

Happy to jump on a 20-min call next week to finalize.

Best,
Alex Rivera
Associate General Counsel (Commercial) | HarborAI
alex.rivera@harborai.com
